name: ProvenMetal

team.summary: Will & Johnny, backed by Y Combinator (S26). Started by assembling circuit boards out of a garage with prosumer grade equipment before pivoting to front of house automation.

product.summary: ProvenMetal delivers assembled circuit boards in 5-7 days by automating front of house workflows (quoting, DFM review using Anthropic in zero-retention mode or manual review, and part procurement via KiCAD and Altium plugins) and coordinating bare board fabs and assembly houses.

market.summary: Domestic PCB supply chain and manufacturing, targeting sectors like drone and defense, where the US global production share dropped from 30% in 2000 to 4% while China dominates at 55%.

risks.risk: High pricing compared to cheap overseas manufacturers in China.
Component sourcing latency and supply chain bottlenecks.
Lack of detailed documentation on manufacturing constraints, layer limits, and precise technical capabilities on the website.

founder_depth.why: Founders experienced the garage assembly constraints firsthand and pivoted their technical approach to software automation and supply chain integration via EDA plugins.

shipping_evidence.why: Took first paying order in less than a week, did roughly $70k across 11 orders in 6 weeks, and built KiCad and Altium plugins.

demand_signal.why: Strong HN engagement with 237 points and 156 comments, plus $70k in early revenue across 11 orders in 6 weeks.

defensibility.why: Relying largely on front-of-house workflow software and partner coordination while hardware manufacturing capacity remains commoditized and capital-intensive.

analysis.verdict_reason: They have impressive initial traction ($70k in 6 weeks) and technical founders who understand the supply chain bottlenecks, though long-term defensibility in hardware brokerage remains a challenge.
would_change_my_mind: Demonstrating sustainable gross margins without relying strictly on defense/ITAR premium pricing
Proving that software automation significantly reduces lead times compared to established domestic competitors
Successfully scaling physical capacity bottlenecks once software automation reaches its limits
data_gaps: Detailed metrics on unit economics and repeat customer retention
Specific partner network agreements and geographic breakdown of fabrication partners
Comprehensive technical capability sheets for advanced layer counts and microvias
